title: The Kuznets curve in the digital age: Understanding inequality dynamics in Europe
decision_rationale: Quantitative panel study of household internet access and S80/S20 income inequality in 28 European countries (family 4), meeting the 10-economy rule for non-AI technology.
exposure_measure: Households with internet access at home (%), Eurostat isoc_ci_in_h (Table 1)

sample.economies_or_groups: 28 European countries (EU members plus Iceland), listed in Section 3.2
sample.income_groups_covered: not reported (European countries; no income-group split)

design.estimator: Fixed-effects threshold panel (Hansen-type), one-step difference/system GMM with imposed threshold, semiparametric GAM
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: Country FE; year FE or trend plus crisis dummies; log GDP per capita PPS and square, GDP growth, tertiary attainment, gender employment gap; alternative control blocks

results.indicator: S80/S20 income quintile share ratio, low-access regime (below 70.78% threshold)
results.estimate: 0.031 (two-way FE preferred); 0.036 (country FE); 0.029 (country FE + trend/crises); per 1 pp internet access
results.uncertainty: clustered SE 0.017 (p = 0.083) in two-way FE; SE 0.016 (p=0.035); SE 0.017 (p=0.097)
results.evidence: Table 2, p.6, row 'Internet access, low regime': 0.031* (0.017)
Table 2, p.6, row 'Internet access, high regime': -0.031*** (0.009); text: 'a 0.31-point decrease above it' per 10 pp

results.estimate: Negative in all six Table 4 models (-0.018 to -0.034), significant in three; low regime not significant (-0.012 to 0.030)
results.uncertainty: robust SE 0.012-0.016 for high-regime; significant in Diff L2-L3, Sys L2-L4, Sys L3-L4
results.evidence: Table 4, p.7; 'GMM partially supports the inequality-reducing mature-diffusion branch'

heterogeneity.finding: Nonlinear stage dependence: positive association below the estimated internet-access threshold (early diffusion), negative above; low branch loses significance when starting year is 2012/2013 and turns negative for 2015-2025

n_specifications_reported: about 30 FE threshold specifications plus 6 GMM, 2 two-step GMM, GAM and cutoff/early-period checks

confounding_reverse_causation.why: FE threshold models have no instrument; GMM uses internal lags with imposed threshold, only partly supportive; authors say results are associations, not causal

exposure_measurement.why: Household internet access share is a coarse access measure, saturating near 99%; no usage or quality

selection_of_countries_years.why: 28 European countries, all relatively high-income, unbalanced 439 observations; low regime identified by early years; 28 clusters

outcome_measurement.why: S80/S20 from Eurostat ilc_di11, harmonized survey measure

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: Threshold estimated by grid search, many control/time variants; authors report all 30 and multiplicity check

selective_reporting.why: Reports all coefficients, null/weak GMM results and fragility of low branch

notes: Outcome is income inequality (family 4) only; no output or productivity outcome. Text states 'we retain the article's fixed-effects threshold framework', suggesting a revised version of an earlier article; no earlier version identified here. Publication dates inside the paper are 2026 with volume year 2027. Only the main text was read to page 9; remaining pages are appendices and references. No instruction-like text found.
